body:
# Build evidence-backed Iranian VPS and managed database discovery

## Problem Statement

Buyers must visit multiple Iranian infrastructure providers to discover configurations, interpret resource and billing differences, and decide which published offer to investigate. The existing traffic-aware VPS comparison helps with one dated, limited sample, but does not provide broad category discovery, managed database discovery, consolidated configurations, provider catalogs, or reproducible search-to-provider journeys.

A cheap published base price is not necessarily a complete bill. Equal hardware does not establish equivalent performance or management responsibilities. Unverified versions, conflicting backup claims, missing mandatory charges and outdated evidence must remain visible rather than becoming false comparison promises.

## Solution

Extend the existing Persian RTL static application into a search-led discovery experience for Iranian VPS and managed databases, kept as separate categories. Include all qualifying managed database offerings from selected sources, without a PostgreSQL-only restriction or a fixed engine whitelist. Select sources through the documented broad coverage search; retain selection reasons and evidence gaps. Compare database prices only within the same engine. Gather broad evidence-backed coverage, consolidate genuinely identical resource configurations across providers, show eligible starting prices, and let buyers inspect individual provider offers before continuing to the provider.

Deliver the full journey: search or browse, narrow results, inspect details and evidence, visit a provider catalog, share or restore the comparison, and leave through a cancellable provider handoff. Preserve the working VPS traffic-aware comparison alongside default base-price discovery.

Coverage has no arbitrary provider/configuration ceiling. Release requires a documented breadth search, reviewed evidence, and at least one genuine exact configuration offered by two or more providers in at least one release category. If broad research cannot establish that match, return the evidence to the human before changing the requirement.

## User Stories

1. As an infrastructure buyer, I want a prominent search box on the homepage, so that I can start with the product I need.
2. As an infrastructure buyer, I want secondary category links, so that I can browse without knowing a product name.
3. As an infrastructure buyer, I want search across product, category and engine names with verified Persian/English aliases, so that familiar terminology finds relevant offers.
4. As an infrastructure buyer, I want VPS and managed database results kept distinct, so that price ordering does not imply equivalent operating responsibilities.
5. As a database buyer, I want engine-name search to find managed offers for that engine, so that I am not redirected to hardware recommendations for running it myself.
6. As an infrastructure buyer, I want broad evidence-backed provider and configuration coverage, so that discovery offers meaningful choice beyond a small demonstration sample.
7. As an infrastructure buyer, I want genuinely matching configurations consolidated into listing items, so that I can compare provider offers for the same resources.
8. As an infrastructure buyer, I want different resource sizes to remain separate, so that approximate size classes do not imply exact matches.
9. As an infrastructure buyer, I want a listing item's starting price calculated from its eligible provider offers, so that its headline reflects my selected constraints.
10. As an infrastructure buyer, I want to inspect individual provider offers within a listing item, so that I can evaluate their actual terms and prices.
11. As a database buyer, I want engine-version filtering backed by evidence on each offer, so that an unsupported or unknown version cannot satisfy my requirement.
12. As an infrastructure buyer, I want minimum-resource filtering, so that larger configurations can remain alternatives when they meet my needs.
13. As an infrastructure buyer, I want exact-resource filtering, so that I can restrict results to the selected amounts.
14. As an infrastructure buyer, I want provider filtering, so that only my selected providers contribute offers and starting prices.
15. As an infrastructure buyer, I want a separate provider profile and catalog, so that I can inspect all its admitted offers at its own prices.
16. As an infrastructure buyer, I want category-specific facets, so that irrelevant controls do not confuse my comparison.
17. As an infrastructure buyer, I want removable filters and result counts, so that I can understand and adjust the current result set.
18. As an infrastructure buyer, I want empty results to preserve my choices and offer recovery, so that constraints are never relaxed silently.
19. As an infrastructure buyer, I want published base prices labelled with currency and billing basis, so that monthly references are not mistaken for complete bills.
20. As an infrastructure buyer, I want base-price budget filtering, so that I can narrow headline prices while seeing that unresolved extras may exceed my budget.
21. As an infrastructure buyer, I want mandatory-charge unknowns distinguished from zero and optional extras, so that missing evidence does not look like a discount.
22. As a VPS buyer, I want default base-price ordering and an explicit traffic-aware mode, so that I can choose the comparison appropriate to my usage.
23. As a VPS buyer, I want editable outbound and optional inbound usage, so that the traffic estimate reflects my scenario.
24. As a VPS buyer, I want traffic arithmetic and units explained, so that I can understand a usage-induced ordering change.
25. As a VPS buyer, I want unknown required traffic charges kept outside ranked subtotals, so that an incomplete estimate does not appear cheapest.
26. As a VPS buyer, I want confirmed hard caps and known paid overage handled correctly, so that suitable paid-overage offers are not rejected and unusable offers are not ranked.
27. As a VPS buyer, I want collapsible usage controls with active assumptions still visible, so that a compact screen does not hide the calculation basis.
28. As a database buyer, I want management, backups, topology, location and feature-package differences available per offer, so that matching hardware does not imply equal service.
29. As an infrastructure buyer, I want visible verification dates and relevant uncertainty warnings, so that I can judge evidence quality before leaving the site.
30. As an infrastructure buyer, I want deeper evidence and source links expandable on demand, so that I can verify facts without overwhelming the results.
31. As an infrastructure buyer, I want stale evidence distinguished from confirmed withdrawal, so that age or a failed page request does not falsely imply an unavailable product.
32. As an infrastructure buyer, I want conflicts to affect only comparisons that depend on the disputed fact, so that unaffected verified facts remain useful.
33. As an infrastructure buyer, I want shareable URLs containing the discovery and comparison state, so that another visit reproduces my view.
34. As an infrastructure buyer, I want reload and browser Back/Forward to restore query, filters, selected detail, usage and mode, so that navigation does not discard my work.
35. As a desktop buyer, I want the configuration list beside a persistent detail pane, so that I can inspect alternatives in context.
36. As a mobile buyer, I want full-width details and Back restoring list position, so that I can investigate an offer and return to browsing.
37. As a mobile buyer, I want filters in a drawer, so that results remain readable on a small screen.
38. As a Persian-speaking buyer, I want readable RTL content, explicit units and accessible controls, so that the full journey is usable on desktop and mobile.
39. As a keyboard user, I want labelled controls and visible focus through filtering, disclosures and navigation, so that I can complete discovery without a mouse.
40. As an infrastructure buyer, I want provider handoff to retain my chosen offer and cost warnings, so that I know what I am investigating and where I am going.
41. As an infrastructure buyer, I want a new-tab handoff with a five-second countdown, Cancel and Continue now, so that I control leaving the site.
42. As an infrastructure buyer, I want a general product/tariff destination disclosed when no exact offer URL is known, so that I do not mistake it for direct checkout.
43. As a catalog maintainer, I want stable provider-offer identities and retained evidence revisions, so that price/name changes and replacement configurations do not rewrite history.
44. As a catalog maintainer, I want a documented search scope and inclusion/exclusion reasons, so that the breadth stopping decision can be assessed.
45. As a catalog maintainer, I want all qualifying published configurations from discovered providers gathered, so that an arbitrary sampling cap does not limit useful coverage.
46. As a catalog maintainer, I want a genuine exact cross-provider match verified before release, so that consolidated comparison is demonstrated with real offers.
47. As a catalog maintainer, I want manual review and catalog validation before publication, so that evidence, eligibility and prices remain consistent.
48. As a catalog maintainer, I want failed verification attempts recorded without advancing successful-verification dates, so that freshness claims stay honest.
49. As a maintainer, I want lean checks of consequential behavior against production and deployed paths, so that delivery is reliable without redundant tests.
50. As the challenge applicant, I want current documentation and a later demonstration outline covering discovery and a traffic-induced ordering change, so that I can explain the delivered value and engineering decisions.
51. As a database buyer, I want all qualifying managed database offerings from selected sources included across their engines, so that discovery is not limited to PostgreSQL.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Architecture:** retain the existing TypeScript/React/Vite static client and reviewed JSON catalog. Manual refresh is sufficient. Extend the catalog validation, comparison operation, discovery UI, URL navigation and delivery checks rather than introducing a backend or replacing working traffic logic.
- **Coverage procedure:** search across both release categories and beyond the historical shortlist. Gather all qualifying published configurations from discovered providers. Within selected sources, inspect and include every qualifying managed database offering across engines; do not stop at PostgreSQL or a small engine sample. Record engine-specific inclusion/exclusion reasons and tariff applicability rather than assuming that a generic database tariff applies to every advertised engine. Stop only after a documented search stops uncovering meaningful additional coverage; retain the search scope, provider inclusion/exclusion reasons and evidence gaps. The earlier two-provider/two-configuration target is superseded as a coverage goal, is not a cap, and is not a sufficient stopping condition. No fixed deadline or effort budget is assumed.
- **Exact-match release gate:** establish at least one sourced exact configuration with offers from two or more providers in at least one release category. Actively seek overlaps under the agreed exact identity rules. If broad search finds none, present its evidence to the human before any relaxation. Do not fabricate offers, merge approximate sizes, or treat synthetic test fixtures as catalog coverage. This gate and broad evidence-backed coverage are independent obligations.
- **Admission:** require an identifiable configuration, public numeric tariff, first-party evidence, source/check date and provider handoff link. A managed database offer also requires documented provider responsibility beyond provisioning, such as maintenance, updates, monitoring, backups or recovery. Ordinary database hosting and customer-installed databases on VPS do not qualify. Unknown mandatory extras can accompany a verified published base price, with incomplete-cost status explicit. A documented but unpriced product is not a catalog offer.
- **Research status:** Liara and ManageIT are initial managed database investigation leads; ArvanCloud is an additional candidate. The historical research does not establish release admission or an exact cross-provider match. Hamravesh's inspected sources did not establish a public numeric tariff; IranServer's standalone managed database was not verified. Recheck evidence rather than treating these historical observations as current facts or permanent exclusions.
- **Offer identity:** preserve stable provider-offer IDs when names or prices change, recording new evidence revisions. Different resource sizes, engines, hardware/feature packages, node topologies, regions and billing variants receive distinct IDs. Preserve earlier configuration evidence rather than rewriting it into a replacement. Version support is evidence on an offer unless sold as distinct configurations.
- **Listing identity:** consolidate by category and exact resource configuration. For databases the key is engine, exact vCPU, RAM, storage capacity/type and node topology, excluding engine version. VPS consolidation likewise requires evidence of matching exact CPU, RAM and storage capacity/type. Unknown identity facts cannot prove a match. Locations, backups, management and version evidence remain visible per offer; grouping never promises equal performance or operating responsibility. Distinct sizes remain separate; no approximate resource bands or size classes.
- **Evidence model:** each offer retains applicable first-party URLs, snapshots or excerpts, check dates, verified facts, explicit unknowns and previous revisions. Preserve conflicting claims and their dates, marking affected facts unresolved until reviewed. Separate source facts, product assumptions and derived calculations. Unknown never means zero, included, unlimited, unavailable or not applicable.
- **Evidence lifecycle:** manually recheck evidence before each catalog release. Evidence becomes stale after 30 days since successful verification; show stale warnings wherever overdue prices appear. Age alone does not remove eligibility. Conflicting or unsuccessfully verified facts cannot satisfy filters or calculations/ranking that depend on them, while unaffected verified facts remain usable. A failed request records an unsuccessful attempt and does not advance the last verified date or prove withdrawal. Changed/disappearing sources trigger review; restore affected eligibility only after verification. Confirmed withdrawal archives the offer and removes it from active offers and price summaries.
- **One eligibility contract:** evolve the public comparison operation to own request/catalog validation, offer-level filtering, evidence-dependent eligibility, listing consolidation, starting prices, traffic calculations, deterministic ordering and reasons for unpriced/excluded offers. Search results, provider catalogs and details consume the same rules; the UI does not independently calculate prices. Keep catalog validity at this boundary and in pre-publication validation.
- **Search:** the homepage leads with search spanning both release categories; category links are secondary and enter the same results experience. Match product, category and engine names with verified Persian/English aliases. Exclude provider names as a search field; use provider filters and profiles. Category selection scopes the query and facets. Provide an engine filter for managed databases, with version choices applicable to the selected engine. Engine-name matching finds that engine's managed offers and does not recommend a VPS merely because it could run that engine. Cross-engine browsing must retain distinct engine identities and separate same-engine price comparisons. Global results retain separate category comparisons rather than a combined cheapest ranking.
- **Resources and versions:** minimum-resource filters require every selected amount to be met or exceeded; exact-resource filters require equality for selected amounts. Unselected amounts impose no requirement. Apply filters to provider offers before calculating listing prices. An unknown or unsupported version fails a requested version filter and cannot supply its starting price. PostgreSQL 18 with at least 2 vCPU / 4 GB may include separate 2 vCPU / 4 GB and 8 vCPU / 64 GB items; exact 2 vCPU / 4 GB excludes the larger item. A PostgreSQL 17-only offer cannot supply the PostgreSQL 18 starting price.
- **Provider discovery:** provider filtering narrows offers within listing items and recomputes their eligible starting prices. Provider profiles show all admitted offers in that provider's release-category catalog at its own prices, even when another provider is cheaper. They do not claim to represent every product the provider sells. Incomplete-cost status applies there as elsewhere.
- **Base prices and budgets:** default to ascending eligible published base prices on a consistent billing basis, labelled as base prices. Price comparison stays within category and, for databases, within the same engine. A budget ceiling applies to each offer's known published base price before starting-price calculation; an offer within it may remain with unknown mandatory charges. Passing this filter is not a complete-bill guarantee. Preserve source billing periods; disclose any monthly-equivalent calculation rather than silently replacing the tariff. Do not invent hourly conversions, caps or minimum charges from wallet-credit prerequisites.
- **Price promises:** distinguish published base price, VPS base-plus-traffic subtotal and total cost. The first two may exclude unresolved mandatory fees only with visible uncertainty. Total-cost ranking requires all mandatory charges known on the stated billing/usage basis; this release does not promise an unconditional complete-cost comparison. An unresolved base tariff cannot contribute a starting price.
- **VPS traffic mode:** default to base-price ordering; make traffic-aware comparison explicit when usage is entered, with the active mode visible. In traffic mode use the cheapest eligible priced provider-offer subtotal for each listing's traffic estimate and ordering. Keep offers with unknown required traffic charges separately inspectable, outside ranked subtotals; a base price must not compete against a usage subtotal. Display base, billable GB, rate, traffic charge and subtotal as applicable, plus incomplete-cost status. Confirmed hard caps exclude; known paid overage charges only excess. Database comparison remains base-price based and never inherits VPS traffic assumptions.
- **Traffic policy continuity:** preserve ManageIT download-as-egress and free upload-as-ingress, using verified applicable rates; preserve the disclosed shared ingress-plus-egress assumption for unspecified-direction allowances while still displaying the source direction as unspecified. These are product interpretations, not newly verified provider facts or user-configurable assumption checkboxes. Retain original wording, policy applicability and evidence. New providers need their own supported terms; do not generalize ManageIT's policy. Unknown required allowance/rate/overage terms cannot manufacture a subtotal.
- **Inputs and units:** preserve optional nonnegative whole-number resource/usage inputs, Persian/Arabic digits, visible validation and safe integer arithmetic. Blank resources impose no constraint and blank usage is zero; 1 TB means 1,000 GB for usage. Preserve advertised resource units and explicit toman amounts. Invalid input must not leave stale matching results on screen. Optional extras remain distinct from mandatory charges.
- **Discovery state:** expose removable filters, result counts, sort and empty-state recovery without silently relaxing constraints. URLs preserve query, category, facets, provider/budget, sort, selected discovery detail, VPS usage and price mode. Sharing/reload and browser Back/Forward restore that comparison. Clean homepage URLs start at defaults. Browser-local persistence is unnecessary. Navigation and restoration must work under the production hosting base path, including handoff URLs.
- **Layout:** implement approved variant C: configuration list and persistent detail pane on desktop, filters above results. Selecting an item reveals eligible provider offers. On mobile use full-width details, Back restoring list position, and filters in a drawer. The throwaway prototype is a design source to preserve, not production code to merge.
- **Progressive disclosure:** keep provider prices, incomplete-cost/conflict/stale warnings and successful-verification dates visible. Expand deeper management responsibilities, backups and source evidence on demand without hiding relevant warnings before handoff. VPS usage controls are collapsible above results, with active assumptions visible while collapsed.
- **Handoff:** open a new tab containing a redirect page identifying the chosen provider/configuration, explaining departure and retaining cost uncertainty. Automatically continue after five seconds; Cancel stops departure and Continue now leaves immediately. Retain the selected offer and reliable destination. If only a general product/tariff URL is known, disclose that limitation and expose source evidence rather than implying direct checkout. A published link does not prove present provisioning availability.
- **Accessibility:** preserve Persian RTL, readable responsive content, labelled controls, keyboard operation and visible focus across search, filters, details, drawer and handoff.
- **Manual publication checklist:** document breadth and inclusion/exclusion decisions; review every configuration's tariff, billing, mandatory extras, traffic and management evidence with reviewer/date; retain snapshots and prior revisions; update facts, conflicts, unknowns and statuses; recompute eligibility and prices; validate identifiers, references, resources/prices and prerequisites; verify breadth and the genuine cross-provider match; publish the reviewed catalog with its evidence history only after release checks pass. Escalate any evidence-backed inability to meet scope before reducing it.
- **Delivery and documentation:** retain the CI test gate, production-build validation and deployed-path smoke verification. Update run/build/test/deployment instructions, coverage/limitations and manual refresh guidance, including the new journeys and restoration behavior. Preserve historical evidence/prototypes as dated assets. Prepare an updated later demonstration outline; recording and submission are subsequent work.

## Testing Decisions

- **Approved seams:** use the existing public comparison operation as the principal domain seam, plus a small set of representative browser journeys through the real application. These seams match the human-approved lean verification in the final release resolution; no additional seam approval or interview is needed. Extend the existing Vitest comparison checks, catalog validation and Playwright desktop/mobile production journeys instead of creating a new testing architecture.
- **Good tests:** assert external decisions and user outcomes: which offers are eligible, which prices contribute, exact arithmetic, uncertainty and reproducible navigation. Avoid private helpers, component structure, layout snapshots, repeated checks at multiple layers and a test for every UI detail. Reuse meaningful existing tests; replace obsolete expectations such as reload clearing state and verification dates being hidden.
- **Domain coverage:** use a compact set of cases for catalog validity and evidence references; exact grouping versus distinct sizes; minimum/exact resources; engine/provider/version/budget eligibility before starting prices and no cross-engine grouping or price ranking; provider-catalog own prices; base-price versus traffic ordering; preserved traffic arithmetic, hard caps and unpriced unknown charges; consequential stale/conflict/failed-verification/withdrawal behavior. Synthetic fixtures may cover edge cases absent in real data, but never enter the release catalog or satisfy the exact-match release gate.
- **Database journey:** search or browse managed databases across admitted engines, narrow to an engine, select a verified version and minimum/exact resources, inspect eligible provider offers and evidence, and hand off. Use a small representative set plus a consequential cross-engine eligibility/grouping check, rather than duplicating a browser suite for every engine. Verify unknown/unsupported versions do not supply results or filtered starting prices, and versions/prices from another engine cannot qualify an offer. PostgreSQL remains a useful example, not the category boundary; do not require PostgreSQL 18 or any other version unless evidence supports it.
- **VPS/provider journey:** browse VPS, filter a provider, inspect its own-price catalog, and exercise a real exact multi-provider item in whichever release category contains it. Confirm provider filtering changes eligible offers and starting prices correctly. Verify the matched item's provider-offer density and disclosures, which were absent from the prototype dataset.
- **Pricing and recovery journey:** switch VPS base/traffic modes, demonstrate a real traffic-induced ordering change and visible arithmetic, and keep unknown required traffic outside ranked subtotals. Exercise the base-price budget with unresolved mandatory extras, then remove/reset filters after no results. Combine these outcomes with the representative journeys rather than duplicating every permutation.
- **Restoration and responsive journey:** share/reload state including selected detail, usage and mode; change filters and use Back/Forward. Check desktop list/detail, mobile drawer/full-width detail and Back restoring list position. Check visible prices/warnings/dates, expandable evidence, RTL, keyboard operation, focus and absence of horizontal overflow in representative flows.
- **Handoff journey:** verify the chosen provider/configuration and destination, general-link disclosure, relevant uncertainty, cancellation, Continue now and automatic five-second continuation. Intercept external navigation where appropriate; no purchase or login is needed.
- **Release verification:** complete the documented broad search, evidence refresh and admission checklist, and verify at least one genuine exact configuration across two or more providers. Automated fixtures and passing browser tests do not establish catalog breadth or real matching offers. Missing real overlap requires returning evidence to the human before relaxing the gate.
- **Production gates:** run type checking, catalog validation, consequential domain checks and representative desktop/mobile journeys against the production artifact at the hosting base path in CI before publication. Smoke-check substantive discovery/restoration/handoff behavior on the deployed path; verify assets and runtime errors. A failed post-deployment check means delivery is not verified even if hosting already published the artifact. Passing checks do not establish current provider capacity or replace the human's layout decision.

## Out of Scope

- Accounts, favorites, saved searches and browser-local persistence.
- Automated ingestion, crawlers, ingestion services, a backend/database and dedicated maintenance tooling.
- Runtime AI and software/workload-to-hardware recommendations.
- International markets and release categories beyond VPS and managed databases.
- Approximate resource bands/size classes, synthetic catalog offers, performance-equivalence claims and combined VPS/database cheapest rankings.
- Unconditional complete-bill guarantees, live capacity/checkout guarantees, provider outreach, account acquisition, login and purchase.
- Recording or submitting the challenge video within this implementation specification; retain the later demonstration outline.

## Further Notes

Scope correction after the initial specification: the user clarified that all qualifying managed database offerings from selected sources belong in the release, not only PostgreSQL. This supersedes the PostgreSQL-only boundary in the historical resolutions and initial spec. Source selection remains governed by the broad evidence-backed search; exact cross-provider matching, admission/evidence requirements and lean testing remain unchanged.

This spec synthesizes the closed [discovery planning map](https://github.com/Fardinak/torob-aipe-challenge/issues/5) and every linked resolution:

- [Managed database evidence resolution](https://github.com/Fardinak/torob-aipe-challenge/issues/6#issuecomment-5750149838) and its [pinned research report](https://github.com/Fardinak/torob-aipe-challenge/blob/32c13717c161036134e55eda114463df195a2ff2/research/managed-database-coverage.md): historical evidence and investigation leads, not admitted offers.
- [Catalog boundary and comparison promises](https://github.com/Fardinak/torob-aipe-challenge/issues/7#issuecomment-6405721272): exact identity, separate services, version eligibility and honest pricing. Its authoritative consolidated resolution incorporates the reopening correction.
- [Search, browsing and reproducibility](https://github.com/Fardinak/torob-aipe-challenge/issues/8#issuecomment-6482092270): search fields, provider catalogs, budget uncertainty and handoff.
- [Evidence and maintenance contract](https://github.com/Fardinak/torob-aipe-challenge/issues/11#issuecomment-6482147787): identity/history, manual review, fact-specific eligibility and visible verification.
- [Layout and interaction resolution](https://github.com/Fardinak/torob-aipe-challenge/issues/9#issuecomment-6482976362), with [pinned prototype](https://github.com/Fardinak/torob-aipe-challenge/blob/277391e/index.html) and [run guide/limits](https://github.com/Fardinak/torob-aipe-challenge/blob/277391e/research/discovery-layout-prototype.md): C, mobile refinements, evidence disclosure and five-second handoff. The artifact did not establish a multi-provider exact match or implement all confirmed refinements.
- [Final scope and specification handoff](https://github.com/Fardinak/torob-aipe-challenge/issues/10#issuecomment-6483980689): supersedes provisional round-one scope, replaces the limited coverage goal, requires real cross-provider overlap and preserves lean verification.

The root CONTEXT.md supplies the domain vocabulary; no ADR directory was present during synthesis. Reconcile the earlier specs/vps-comparison.md and README guidance during implementation: expand the VPS-only sample scope, replace memory-only/reload-reset behavior with URL restoration, include discovery/detail/provider views, expose successful-verification dates despite the old timestamp exclusion, and preserve traffic interpretations as disclosed product assumptions. Historical research and prototype assets remain clearly dated rather than rewritten as current release evidence.

The later demonstration should show the buyer's discovery problem, search/category entry, narrowing, offer/evidence inspection and provider handoff, plus a VPS traffic-induced ordering change and relevant engineering/AI-assisted development decisions.

This handoff does not claim that broad acquisition, refreshed tariffs, release-admitted database coverage, a genuine cross-provider match, implementation or release verification are already complete. Newly discovered scope decisions return to the human with evidence.
title: Build evidence-backed Iranian VPS and managed database discovery
